newsitem.title: UK: Britain approves Shell, Elf oil/gas developments.
newsitem.headline: Britain approves Shell, Elf oil/gas developments.

text.p: The British government said on Thursday it granted Shell UK and France's Elf approval to develop three North Sea gas condensate fields and build a pipeline to a gas terminal in eastern England.

A government statement said Energy Minister Lord Fraser gave his consent to Shell UK to develop the Shearwater gas field. He also approved Elf Aquitaine's development of the neighbouring Elgin and Franklin gas fields.
First production is expected early in 2000.
The pipeline, named the Shearwater and Elgin Area Line (SEAL), will be the longest on the UK Continental Shelf at 463 km (288 miles), the statement said.
It will carry gas from the three fields, located some 230 km (143 miles) east of Aberdeen in Scotland, to an existing terminal at Bacton in eastern England.
From there, the gas will be sent to the Transco National Transmission System (NTS) and to Europe through the Bacton to Zeebrugge interconnector pipeline.
Construction is expected to begin in 1998 with first gas expected to flow in 2000.
